item.title: The AI Researcher Who Just Quit Anthropic Says It’s ‘Crunch Time for Humanity’
item.description: Jacob Coxon talks to WIRED about the “mini Manhattan project” inside Anthropic, the problem with alignment, and why AI labs have just a few years left to make their systems safe.

item.title: San Francisco Orders Meta to Stop ‘Allowing’ AI Child Abuse Ads
item.description: The City Attorney’s Office has asked Meta to explain how the harmful ads repeatedly ran on Facebook and Instagram. The company claims the ads are not under the city’s jurisdiction.

item.title: I Let an AI Agent Hack All My Gadgets—and I’d Do It Again
item.description: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC. But it also told me how to make everything a lot more secure.

item.title: A Stealth Startup Thinks It Just Hacked the Memory Shortage
item.description: Kepler Computing claims a new approach to chip design—and a proprietary material—can help end the supply bottlenecks that have sent memory prices surging.

item.title: Muse, Meta’s New Personal AI Agent, Needs You to Trust It
item.description: Designed to compete with OpenClaw and Instinct, the company says Muse can do everything from sell your car to book you a plane ticket.

item.title: OpenAI Just Claimed a Huge Math Discovery. Some Academics Are Crying Foul
item.description: A landmark announcement by the frontier AI lab has been overshadowed by accusations of impropriety.

item.title: Whispering Complaints Into Your Phone May Be the Future of Customer Feedback
item.description: Forget email surveys or long calls spent on hold. Voicebox lets people send customer feedback by recording a voice note on their phone.

item.title: My Brief Summer Fling With Siri AI
item.description: I was initially enamored with the beta version of Apple’s revamped smartphone assistant. As the full release approaches, I’ve forgotten Siri AI even exists.

item.title: Why China Is the Bogeyman Data Center Enthusiasts Just Can’t Quit
item.description: Polls show that overwhelming majorities of Americans hate data centers. China makes a perfect scapegoat for tech leaders and their allies—the only problem is a lack of evidence.

item.title: OpenAI Agents Hacked Another Website
item.description: Plus: Tens of millions of US and Canadian drivers’ licenses go up for sale on the dark web, the US military finally tries to tackle the risk online ad data poses to troops, and more.
